result.title: Provenance Signatures for Low Rank Adaptations of Image Diffusion Models
result.summary: Diffusion models have revolutionized the generation of realistic artificial images. Efficient techniques such as Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA) can modify these models for particular use cases, making them more diverse and widely usable. At the same time, open base models may be adapted to deliver biased, harmful or illegal images in an online service. In this paper, we develop a protocol to detect when a service may be using an adaptation of an otherwise standard model. We describe the precise setup and threat model for this provenance question and define two different problems arising due the presence of multiple model families and multiple adaptations. In contrast to previous works that have considered model identification within lists of known candidate models, we consider the realistic open world scenario where the set of possible adaptations and alternative models are unknown. Using a hypothesis testing approach, our protocols can distinguish between the base model, a LoRA adaptation and other completely different families of models. For this test, we develop a black box signature of the models based only on intrinsic dimension of sets of images generated by the models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出面向图像扩散模型 LoRA 适配的溯源协议，在开放世界威胁模型下用基于生成图像集合内在维度的黑箱签名，区分基础模型、LoRA 适配与其它模型族。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作属图像生成模型的归属检测，与 VLM 推理中的视觉证据使用、latent 状态生成与停止决策无实质联系；内在维度签名虽涉及表示几何统计，但用途是模型指纹识别而非推理状态分析，缺少可供核查的具体借鉴线索。
